title: Storage house: receiving, dispatch and protected logistics progression
retained_base: Accepted starter/reinforced/advanced house and organization references remain historical selected forms. Typed bays, fuel separation and central access already exist; they are not new purchases.

stages.name: DISPATCH WAREHOUSE
stages.baseline_limitation: The existing house has organized typed stock but a small shared receiving/collection frontage.
stages.appearance_change: Keep the familiar house core and central front blue sliding doors; add a substantial left receiving wing and covered unloading apron, a separate front-left dispatch canopy, sturdy expanded shelving and physical reserved-order staging cages.
stages.purchase_value: Receiving and dispatch use separate reachable positions, allowing a supplier and collector to work simultaneously without occupying the same doorway. Practical bounded building storage may expand after actual capacity tuning; actor carry remains unlimited.
stages.input_processing_output: Incoming worker or conveyor cargo remains unaccepted until custody commits. Accepted goods join the one existing typed-stock ledger. Reserved goods remain owned stock staged for a specific outgoing job until pickup commits; they are not a duplicated inventory. Existing resource identities never change.
stages.jobs: Bulk receive, put away, reserve a specific job load, retrieve and dispatch while another living worker receives. Right fuel hatch remains a separate fuel route.
stages.footprint_ports_clearance: Purchased left-wing expansion and front apron; original central front sliding doors remain clear for pedestrian/manual access; a separate front-left dispatch hatch belongs to the new wing, central pedestrian aisle stays clear, right fuel service never crosses the public stock queue.
stages.tradeoff: More land and construction/repair cost; finite receiving/dispatch positions need reservations. A full or destroyed destination blocks transfer and leaves custody with the delivering actor.
requirements: Separate receiving and dispatch reservations plus custody commit
Reachable construction bill and upgrade migration of existing stock
One stock ledger: inbound-unaccepted cargo, accepted typed stock, reserved outgoing stock and committed departure are distinct custody states, never copied counts.

stages.name: LOGISTICS HALL
stages.baseline_limitation: One receiving bay and one dispatch zone constrain several producers, crews and garage deliveries.
stages.appearance_change: A much larger twin-gable timber-and-blue warehouse with a robust stone base, distinct covered receiving and dispatch bays, a clear central pedestrian aisle, high typed racks, a hand-operated gantry/loading hoist and a protected order-staging zone. Preserve the recognizable original house facade as the central core. The hand hoist and its consistent rail/trolley sit over the LEFT receiving-to-dispatch handling path with a reachable hand chain/crank, never in an unrelated right-side bay.
stages.purchase_value: Independent intake and dispatch reservations support multiple useful jobs and segregated pending orders. A loading hoist shortens real pickup/placement handling once implemented; stronger walls and shutters provide finite protection while leaving stock recoverable after destruction.
stages.input_processing_output: Goods enter a real receiving opening in the LEFT WALL, commit into one typed stock ledger, and reserved goods leave a separate FRONT-LEFT dispatch hatch. Both rear walls are solid. Right-side fuel has its own isolated service hatch. Worker and eligible standard conveyor handoffs only; no direct warehouse truck unload or VC01 transfer-policy decision.
stages.jobs: Receiving, put-away, dispatch and loading can be assigned concurrently to eligible living workers; no automatic staff appears.
stages.footprint_ports_clearance: Purchased wider/deeper twin-bay hall, real left-wall receiving opening and front-left dispatch hatch, solid rear walls, original central front sliding-door pedestrian aisle kept clear. The hand hoist serves only the left stock path; right fuel service remains isolated. No direct truck unloading.
stages.tradeoff: Large plot and repair commitment; concurrent jobs require safe approach space, real labor/operation rules and destination capacity. It is not invulnerable or infinite logical building storage by implication.
requirements: Shared stock reservations with per-order staging and no duplicate custody
Bounded warehouse capacity contract if adopted; exact units unapproved
Garage-first and unresolved VC01 policy remain external; no direct warehouse truck unload is introduced
HP/ruin/salvage, protected access and expanded plot migration
Unaccepted inbound stock stays with its real owner; reservations do not clone stock; outgoing custody commits once at pickup.

ordered_inputs.role: Selected advanced house is retained architectural identity, including warm timber, pitched roof, central front blue sliding doors and separated fuel hatch. New wings are explicit authored expansion, not an overwritten old form.
Existing typed organization and central aisle already belong to baseline. Keep those functions and add real receiving/dispatch separation, concurrent access and loading handling.
Owner-selected ordinary raw-resource and cash scale. This sheet does not establish the processed plank or fuel identity; use selected 04 for those.
Selected processed resources, including existing planks, meal and fuel forms. Preserve each pictured product identity and approved unit size.

prompt: Create a strong HAVENLINE World 1 purchase-value upgrade concept sheet, using the supplied references as the retained base identity and scale anchors. Chunky rounded stylized 3D mobile-game art: warm orange timber, deep blue painted metal, rounded gray hardware and softly sculpted snow. Clean navy studio ground, controlled lighting and clear silhouettes. The upgrades must visibly add working structure and a useful operation, not just thicker brackets or a recolor. Make EXACTLY two rows by three roomy columns, six substantial panels. Top row is the first new proposal; bottom row is the later new proposal. Within each row show the SAME physical design in exterior front three-quarter, genuine opposite rear three-quarter, and an open/cutaway functional view. Keep a consistent scale and physical coordinate system within each row. The functional view is the same object with roof/guard hidden, never an extra design. Preserve approved ordinary resource size and standard conveyor width/height. Bigger buildings and new ports are authored upgrades with clear purchased ground area, not enlarged resources or a new belt skin. Do not show the old base as a newly designed third stage. Titles and short stage/view labels only; no numerical levels, prices, yields, capacity or rate claims. Footer: AUTHORED UPGRADE PROPOSAL. No workers, UI, magic energy, electric fields or unsupported fuel system. This is proposed design, not proof of runtime implementation. HEADER: HAVENLINE / STORAGE HOUSE PROGRESSION. Existing references already have typed organization; the new purchase value must be visibly larger physical workflow. TOP ROW label DISPATCH WAREHOUSE. Preserve a recognizable central timber house with blue roof and central front blue sliding doors, then add a substantial left receiving wing with its own covered unloading apron. Add a separate front-left dispatch canopy and clearly distinct physical reserved-order staging racks. Keep a broad unobstructed central pedestrian aisle and the isolated right-side fuel hatch. Goods enter from the object LEFT wing and depart at the separate FRONT-LEFT dispatch hatch in the new wing; the original central front doors remain clear; these positions do not mirror between views. BOTTOM ROW label LOGISTICS HALL. Make a decisive larger twin-gable warehouse with stone lower protection, blue frames, tall typed racks, separate covered receiving and dispatch bays, a practical hand-operated gantry/hoist over a loading cradle and an open pedestrian corridor. The original house facade remains recognizable in the central core. Receiving is through an actual opening in the object LEFT WALL, dispatch through the FRONT-LEFT hatch, fuel service at the RIGHT exterior hatch; all REAR walls remain solid; leave separate outside aprons for each and no crossing through the central pedestrian aisle. Shutters and low protective walls must not seal the working doors. In the third panel of each row peel away the FRONT FACADE and near roof plane for the cutaway to show the SAME interior: receiving stock, typed holding racks, reserved dispatch staging and clear aisle must connect physically. Put a few correctly scaled representative material/food/timber/fuel bundles in distinct bays, with food storage only and fuel apart. Show storage containers and a loading cradle, not giant decorative resource piles. No people or vehicle required; keep space for ordinary workers and approved conveyor interfaces; do not depict or imply a direct truck-unloading bay. Short view captions FRONT / REAR / CUTAWAY. No cash generation, food-processing machinery, magical conveyor-through-wall connection or numerical storage labels. The original central front sliding-door opening and its entire pedestrian aisle must remain unblocked; dispatch uses its own front-left hatch, not that opening. Draw separate receiving, accepted typed stock and reserved outgoing physical zones without multiplying the same goods. Only worker or compatible standard conveyor handoffs; no direct truck unloading at this building. Place the manual loading hoist ON THE LEFT stock-handling route between receiving and reserved dispatch. Show one consistent rail/trolley, a reachable hand chain or crank, and a useful stock cradle in every angle. Do not invent an extra front-right general-cargo port beside fuel. The functional view peels away the real front facade/roof; do not relocate the blue central sliding doors to a rear wall or create doors blocked by shelves. Selected processed fuel is the orange handled X-panel unit in reference 04; use its actual identity. The left-wall receiving bay must be an actually EMPTY walkable doorway/threshold into a reachable receiving floor, not a sign placed over a full shelf or a fake painted opening. Keep stock racks away from its threshold.
acceptance_checks: Existing typed bays not mislabeled as a newly purchased capability
Clear exterior growth from house to receiving/dispatch warehouse to twin-bay logistics hall
Separate receiving and dispatch positions actually connect to reachable typed bays
Central pedestrian aisle, front exit and right fuel route remain clear
Hoist and staging zones are functional structures, not decorative trim
All three views match each physical stage, including roof/bay/fuel-hatch placement
No invented actor carrying cap, free goods/cash or settled garage transfer policy
Accepted starter/reinforced/advanced source images remain untouched
Actual left-wall receiving opening and front-left dispatch hatch, with solid rear walls
Cutaway peels the real front facade; central blue doors are not moved to a blocked rear wall
Hoist has one consistent left-side rail/trolley and reachable manual actuator, useful stock route and clear pedestrian aisle
Left receiving doorway has an empty usable threshold and floor route; no shelf or sign masquerades as the opening.
